AI.summary: 本文针对互联非线性动力系统，提出了一种基于Lyapunov的固定时间输入到状态稳定（FxT-ISS）小增益定理，并通过非光滑反馈控制器在实时优化和博弈纳什均衡寻优中得到了成功应用。
AI.keywords: 固定时间输入到状态稳定, Lyapunov小增益定理, 非线性互联系统, 实时反馈优化, 纳什均衡寻优
AI.comments: 本文在非线性互联系统稳定理论方面取得了重要进展，首次将小增益定理推广到了固定时间输入到状态稳定（FxT-ISS）框架下，并通过反馈优化和博弈论中的纳什均衡寻优展示了极强的应用潜力。其局限性或未来方向在于如何进一步减少对非光滑控制器的依赖或降低实际工程实施中的计算复杂度。

title: Benchmarking Learning-Based Formula 1 Race Strategies
summary: This paper presents two complementary frameworks to optimize Formula 1 race strategies, jointly accounting for energy allocation, tire wear and pit stop timing. First, the race scenario is modeled using lap time maps and a dynamic tire wear model capturing the main trade-offs arising during a race. Then, we solve the problem by means of a mixed-integer nonlinear program that handles the integer nature of the pit stop decisions. The same race scenario is embedded into a reinforcement learning environment, on which an agent is trained. Providing fast inference at runtime, this method is suited to improve human decision-making during real races. The learned policy's suboptimality is assessed with respect to the optimal solution, both in a nominal scenario and with an unforeseen disturbance. In both cases, the agent achieves approximately 5s of suboptimality on 1.5h of race time, mainly attributable to the different energy allocation strategy. This work lays the foundations for learning-based race strategies and provides a benchmark for future developments.

AI.title_translation: 基于学习的一级方程式赛车策略基准测试
AI.tldr: 本文提出并基准测试了基于混合整数规划和强化学习的F1赛车策略优化框架，证明了强化学习在实时比赛决策中的高效性。
AI.motivation: 为了优化一级方程式（Formula 1）赛车策略，同时兼顾能量分配、轮胎磨损和进站时机，并克服传统方法无法兼顾计算速度与实时决策支持的局限性。
AI.method: 首先使用单圈时间图和动态轮胎磨损模型对比赛场景进行建模，并通过混合整数非线性规划（MINLP）求解最优解；其次，将该场景嵌入强化学习环境中训练智能体，实现运行时的快速推理。
AI.result: 在名义场景和遭遇意外干扰的场景下，经训练的强化学习智能体在1.5小时的比赛时间中，其表现与最优解的差距约为5秒，该差距主要归因于能量分配策略的不同。
AI.conclusion: 基于学习的策略在1.5小时的比赛中与最优解的差距仅约为5秒，证明了强化学习在实时F1比赛策略优化中的可行性与高效性，为未来的发展提供了坚实的基准。

title: Embodied Learning of Reward for Musculoskeletal Control with Vision Language Models
summary: Discovering effective reward functions remains a fundamental challenge in motor control of high-dimensional musculoskeletal systems. While humans can describe movement goals explicitly such as "walking forward with an upright posture," the underlying control strategies that realize these goals are largely implicit, making it difficult to directly design rewards from high-level goals and natural language descriptions. We introduce Motion from Vision-Language Representation (MoVLR), a framework that leverages vision-language models (VLMs) to bridge the gap between goal specification and movement control. Rather than relying on handcrafted rewards, MoVLR iteratively explores the reward space through iterative interaction between control optimization and VLM feedback, aligning control policies with physically coordinated behaviors. Our approach transforms language and vision-based assessments into structured guidance for embodied learning, enabling the discovery and refinement of reward functions for high-dimensional musculoskeletal locomotion and manipulation. These results suggest that VLMs can effectively ground abstract motion descriptions in the implicit principles governing physiological motor control.

title: MedGemma vs GPT-4: Open-Source and Proprietary Zero-shot Medical Disease Classification from Images
comments: Accepted for publication in the Journal of Machine Learning and Deep Learning (JMLDL). 9 pages, 9 figures, 10 tables
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce an emerging paradigm for medical imaging by interpreting scans through the lens of extensive clinical knowledge, offering a transformative approach to disease classification. This study presents a critical comparison between two fundamentally different AI architectures: the specialized open-source agent MedGemma and the proprietary large multimodal model GPT-4 for diagnosing six different diseases. The MedGemma-4b-it model, fine-tuned using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), demonstrated superior diagnostic capability by achieving a mean test accuracy of 80.37% compared to 69.56% for the untuned GPT-4. Furthermore, MedGemma exhibited notably higher sensitivity in high-stakes clinical tasks, such as cancer and pneumonia detection. Quantitative analysis via confusion matrices and classification reports provides comprehensive insights into model performance across all categories. These results emphasize that domain-specific fine-tuning is essential for minimizing hallucinations in clinical implementation, positioning MedGemma as a sophisticated tool for complex, evidence-based medical reasoning.

title: A pumping-like lemma for languages over infinite alphabets
summary:
We prove a pumping-like lemma for languages accepted by one-register alternating finite-memory automata over an infinite alphabet. Every sufficiently long accepted word has a nonempty factor in a bounded suffix that can be repeated under successive powers of a single alphabet permutation. The proof analyzes accepting runs backwards, counting register values by their state profiles within the remaining suffix and summarizing values outside it.
  We derive effective semi-linearity of the sets of accepted word lengths and prove non-closure under reversal, concatenation, and Kleene star. We also show that this pumping lemma cannot be extended to alternating automata with two registers.

title: SelfGRL: Self-Organized Graph Representation Learning Inspired by Helmholtz Free Energy Minimization
comments: Submitted to The ACM Web Conference 2027 (WWW 2027)
summary: Graph Representation Learning (GRL) requires node embeddings to preserve local structural coherence while remaining globally discriminative. Existing graph self-supervised methods generally coordinate these competing objectives through method-specific designs, lacking a unified and adaptive mechanism that responds to the evolving representation state. To address this limitation, we propose SelfGRL, a self-organized graph representation learning framework that reformulates representation learning as Helmholtz free-energy minimization on the unit hypersphere. SelfGRL models local neighborhood attraction as a Structural Binding Energy through neighbor-mean alignment, while introducing a Sampling-Free Repulsive Entropy objective to preserve global dispersion and prevent representation collapse without pairwise negative sampling. To dynamically coordinate these competing effects, we develop an endogenous Bayesian Thermostat that adaptively regulates their relative strengths in response to the evolving representation state, allowing the system to approach a metastable semantic equilibrium without requiring manually tuned loss weights. Extensive experiments on node classification across both homophilic and heterophilic benchmark datasets, together with link prediction evaluations, demonstrate that SelfGRL consistently achieves strong performance across diverse graph structures.

title: On the burst-covering radius of binary cyclic codes
summary: We define and study burst-covering codes. We provide some general bounds connecting the parameters of a code with its burst-covering radius. We then provide stronger bounds on the burst-covering radius of cyclic codes, by employing linear-feedback shift-register (LFSR) sequences. For the case of BCH codes we prove a bound on pattern frequencies in LFSR sequences, and using this tool, we bound the burst-covering radius of binary primitive BCH codes and Melas codes. We then present an efficient burst-covering algorithm for cyclic codes. Finally, we present a bound on the critical exponent of cyclic codes based on the burst-covering radius.

title: The asymptotic size of finite irreducible semigroups of rational matrices
comments: full version of a STACS'26 paper, invited for a special issue of LMCS, revision based on referee reports
summary:
In this paper we investigate the maximum size of finite semigroups of rational $n \times n$ matrices, with the goal of shedding more light on their structure. Such semigroups provide a rich generalisation of transition monoids of unambiguous (and, in particular, deterministic) finite automata. While in general such semigroups can be arbitrarily large in terms of $n$, a classical result of Schützenberger from 1962 implies an upper bound of $2^{O(n^2 \log n)}$ for irreducible semigroups. A semigroup of rational matrices is called irreducible if the only subspaces of $\mathbb{Q}^n$ that are invariant for all matrices in the semigroup are $\mathbb{Q}^n$ and the subspace consisting only of the zero vector. Irreducible matrix semigroups can be viewed as the building blocks of general matrix semigroups, and as such play an important role in mathematics and computer science. From the point of view of automata theory, they can be seen as a generalisation of strongly connected weighted automata.
  Using a very different technique from that of Schützenberger, we improve the upper bound on the cardinality to $3^{n^2}$. This is the main result of the paper. The bound is in some sense tight, as we show that there exists, for every $n$, a finite irreducible semigroup with $3^{\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor}$ rational matrices. Our main result also leads to an improvement of a bound, due to Almeida and Steinberg, on the mortality threshold of finite semigroups of rational matrices. The mortality threshold is a number $\ell$ such that if the zero matrix is in the semigroup, then the zero matrix can be written as a product of at most $\ell$ matrices from any subset that generates the semigroup.

title: Octopus: Agentic Multi-Table Discovery over Tabular Data Lakes
comments: Substantial redesign of Octopus as an agentic framework
summary: Tabular data discovery aims to identify the tables relevant to a natural-language question from a large collection of heterogeneous data. Existing systems typically assume that a question is answered by a single table and rely on retrieval pipelines constructed through substantial offline preprocessing. These assumptions become restrictive when relevant information is distributed across multiple tables. In this paper, we present Octopus, a lightweight agentic framework for multi-table data discovery. Octopus follows a thin-harness design that combines lightweight offline semantic guidance with adaptive access to raw tabular data. At query time, an LLM agent dynamically orchestrates semantic column search, structured tabular operations, and general-purpose execution to locate and verify relevant tables based on intermediate observations. We further introduce a benchmark that explicitly evaluates multi-table data discovery, covering both settings where multiple tables independently answer a question and settings where multiple tables must be joined. Experimental results across four independent-discovery datasets and two join-based datasets show that Octopus achieves the highest macro-F1 on all six datasets. It also substantially reduces offline preprocessing overhead relative to Pneuma and online latency and API cost relative to Claude Code. When coupled with the same NL2SQL agent, Octopus yields substantially higher downstream question-answering F1 than Claude Code, showing that improved table discovery provides more complete evidence for downstream analytics. Code is available at https://github.com/wenzhilics/octopus.

title: Self-Learning Surprise Detection in Spatial Audio for Viewport-Aware 360-Video Streaming
comments: Accepted at IEEE ICME 2026. 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted manuscript; replaces the v2 withdrawal notice
summary: Adaptive streaming of 360-degree video relies on viewport prediction to allocate bandwidth efficiently. Current approaches predominantly use visual saliency or historical gaze patterns, neglecting the role of spatial audio in guiding user attention. This paper presents a self-learning framework for detecting "surprising" auditory events, moments that deviate from learned temporal expectations, and demonstrates their utility for viewport prediction. The proposed architecture combines SE(3)-equivariant graph neural networks with recurrent temporal modeling, trained via a dual self-supervised objective. A key feature is the natural modeling of temporal attention decay: surprise is high at event onset but diminishes as the listener adapts. Experiments on the AVTrack360 dataset show that integrating audio surprise with visual cues reduces bitrate waste by up to 18% compared to visual-only methods.

title: Sandwich Reasoning: An Answer-Reasoning-Answer Approach for Low-Latency Query Correction
summary: Query correction is a critical entry point in modern search pipelines, demanding high accuracy strictly within real-time latency constraints. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning improves accuracy but incurs prohibitive latency for real-time query correction. A potential solution is to output an answer before reasoning to reduce latency; however, under autoregressive decoding, the early answer is independent of subsequent reasoning, preventing the model from leveraging its reasoning capability to improve accuracy. To address this issue, we propose Sandwich Reasoning (SandwichR), a novel approach that explicitly aligns a fast initial answer with post-hoc reasoning, enabling low-latency query correction without sacrificing reasoning-aware accuracy. SandwichR follows an Answer-Reasoning-Answer paradigm, producing an initial correction, an explicit reasoning process, and a final refined correction. To align the initial answer with post-reasoning insights, we design a consistency-aware reinforcement learning (RL) strategy: a dedicated consistency reward enforces alignment between the initial and final corrections, while margin-based rejection sampling prioritizes borderline samples where reasoning drives the most impactful corrective gains. Additionally, we construct a high-quality query correction dataset, addressing the lack of specialized benchmarks for complex query correction. Experimental results demonstrate that SandwichR achieves SOTA accuracy comparable to standard CoT while delivering a 40-70% latency reduction, resolving the latency-accuracy trade-off in online search.

title: A Highly Efficient Diversity-based Input Selection for DNN Improvement Using VLMs
summary: Maintaining or improving the performance of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) through fine-tuning requires labeling newly collected inputs, a process that is often costly and time-consuming. To alleviate this problem, input selection approaches have been developed in recent years to identify small, yet highly informative subsets for labeling. Diversity-based selection is one of the most effective approaches for this purpose. However, they are often computationally intensive and lack scalability for large input sets, limiting their practical applicability. To address this challenge, we introduce Concept-Based Diversity (CBD), a novel and highly efficient diversity metric for image inputs that leverages Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Our results show that CBD exhibits a strong correlation with Geometric Diversity (GD), an established diversity metric, while requiring only a fraction of its computation time. Building on this finding, we propose a hybrid input selection approach that combines CBD with Margin, a simple uncertainty metric. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation across a diverse set of DNN models, input sets, selection budgets, and six most effective state-of-the-art selection baselines. The results demonstrate that the CBD-based selection consistently outperforms all baselines at guiding input selection to improve the DNN model. Furthermore, the CBD-based selection approach remains highly efficient, requiring selection times close to those of simple uncertainty-based methods such as Margin, even on larger input sets like ImageNet. These results confirm not only the effectiveness and computational advantage of the CBD-based approach, particularly compared to hybrid baselines, but also its scalability in repetitive and extensive input selection scenarios.

title: Maximizing R{é}nyi Entropy over the Transportation Polytope: Structure and Algorithm
summary: We study the problem of finding the minimum $\mathbb{L}\_2$-norm element in a transportation polytope. It corresponds to minimizing the index of coincidence or maximizing R{é}nyi entropy over joint probability distributions with prescribed marginals. The solution is straightforward under a feasibility condition on the marginals. We make three contributions. First, we decompose the basic solution into a mixture of three interpretable couplings and derive a closed-form sampling procedure, revealing its role as the $\mathbb{L}\_2$-projection of the uniform distribution onto the transportation polytope. Second, we show that the feasibility condition becomes exponentially rare as the number of modalities grows, which highlights the practical necessity of a more general construction. Third, we provide a KKT-based iterative construction of the optimal coupling for arbitrary marginals with explicit Lagrange multipliers.

title: Parallelizable memory recurrent units
comments: This work has been the subject of patent applications (Numbers: EP26151077 and EP26175248.9)
summary: With the emergence of massively parallel processing units, parallelization has become a desirable property for new sequence models. The ability to parallelize the processing of sequences with respect to the sequence length during training is one of the main factors behind the uprising of the Transformer architecture. However, Transformers lack efficiency at sequence generation, as they need to reprocess all past timesteps at every generation step. Recently, state-space models (SSMs) emerged as a more efficient alternative. These new kinds of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) keep the efficient update of the RNNs while gaining parallelization by getting rid of nonlinear dynamics (or recurrence). SSMs can reach state-of-the-art performance through the efficient training of potentially very large networks, but still suffer from limited representation capabilities. In particular, SSMs cannot exhibit persistent memory, or the capacity of retaining information for an infinite duration, because of their monostability. In this paper, we introduce a new family of RNNs, the memory recurrent units (MRUs), that combine the persistent memory capabilities of nonlinear RNNs with the parallelizable computations of SSMs. These units leverage multistability as a source of persistent memory, while getting rid of transient dynamics for efficient computations. We then derive a specific implementation as proof-of-concept: the bistable memory recurrent unit (BMRU). This new RNN is compatible with the parallel scan algorithm. We show that BMRU achieves good results in tasks with long-term dependencies, and can be combined with SSMs to create parallelizable hybrid networks that have both transient dynamics and persistent memory.

title: Beyond the Dirac Delta: Mitigating Diversity Collapse in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Versatile Image Generation
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a paradigm for fine-tuning large-scale generative models, such as diffusion and flow models, to align with complex human preferences and user-specified tasks. A fundamental limitation remains \textit{the curse of diversity collapse}, where the objective formulation and optimization landscape inherently collapse the policy to a Dirac delta distribution. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{DRIFT} (\textbf{D}ive\textbf{R}sity-\textbf{I}ncentivized Reinforcement \textbf{F}ine-\textbf{T}uning for Versatile Image Generation), an innovative framework that systematically incentivizes output diversity throughout the on-policy fine-tuning process, reconciling strong task alignment with high generation diversity to enhance versatility essential for applications that demand diverse candidate generations. We approach the problem across three representative perspectives: i) \textbf{sampling} a reward-concentrated subset that filters out reward outliers to prevent premature collapse; ii) \textbf{prompting} with stochastic variations to expand the conditioning space, and iii) \textbf{optimization} of the intra-group diversity with a potential-based reward shaping mechanism. Experimental results show that DRIFT exhibits clear Pareto dominance in task alignment and generation diversity, achieving 3.88\%$\sim$81.42\% higher diversity at matched alignment and 14.38\%$\sim$56.45\% higher alignment at matched diversity. Our code is available at \textcolor{magenta}{\href{https://github.com/NJU-RL/DRIFT}{https://github.com/NJU-RL/DRIFT}}.

title: RoSeViT: Role-Separated Vision Transformers for ARC Visual Reasoning
comments: NeurIPS 2026 poster (camera-ready). Code, checkpoints and predictions: https://github.com/lz7fd/RoSeViT
summary: ARC tasks can be formulated as visual transformation problems, where a model must infer a high-level transformation rule from a small set of demonstrations and apply it consistently across a grid. While dense Vision Transformers (ViTs) perform well in this setting, they entangle local visual state and global transformation logic within a shared token representation, which can hinder consistent reasoning. In this paper, we introduce RoSeViT, a role-separated Vision Transformer that explicitly decouples high-level instruction inference from visual workspace computation. RoSeViT uses controller tokens to aggregate transformation-level information and workspace tokens to represent the visual grid, with a structured attention pass in which nonlocal workspace interactions are routed through the controller. This design is motivated by our formal analysis showing that enforcing a shared instruction representation can reduce the effective complexity of visual transformation modeling. RoSeViT outperforms dense ViT baselines under the standard VARC training and evaluation protocol for ARC. In a controlled backbone replacement setting, it improves ARC-1 accuracy from 54.5 to 56.6, and with recurrent refinement reaches 58.8. When integrated into the full system, RoSeViT-Ensemble improves performance from 60.4 to 62.6 on ARC-1. These results demonstrate that explicitly separating instruction and workspace representations leads to more effective visual reasoning on ARC tasks. GitHub repository: https://github.com/lz7fd/RoSeViT.

title: Data-Driven Safe Output Regulation of Strict-Feedback Linear Systems with Input Delay
summary: This paper develops a data-driven safe control framework for linear systems possessing a known strict-feedback structure, but with most plant parameters, external disturbances, and input delay being unknown. By leveraging Koopman operator theory, we utilize Krylov dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to extract the system dynamics from measured data, enabling the reconstruction of the system and disturbance matrices. Concurrently, the batch least-squares identification (BaLSI) method is employed to identify other unknown parameters in the input channel. Using control barrier functions (CBFs) and backstepping, we first develop a full-state safe controller. Based on this, we build an output-feedback controller by performing system identification using only the output data and actuation signals as well as constructing an observer to estimate the unmeasured plant states. The proposed approach achieves: 1) finite-time identification of a substantial set of unknown system quantities, and 2) exponential convergence of the output state (the state furthest from the control input) to a reference trajectory while rigorously ensuring safety constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a safe vehicle platooning application.

title: Referential Regimes: Transformation-Based Identity Profiles for Neutral Substrates
comments: 60 pages; revised manuscript with Lean 4-certified transformation classifications and formal results characterizing equality and separation of invariant-preserving step-generated identity relations. Companion Lean 4 formalization available on GitHub
summary:
Data systems operating under persistent legal, institutional, and analytic disagreement require shared reference without presupposing agreement about interpretation. This paper investigates identity preservation under transformation, building on the conditional neutrality result of Neutral Substrates (arXiv:2601.14271).
  We pair candidate identity bases with families of record transformations and classify each family as preserving, breaking, neutral, or inapplicable for a basis. Using invariant-defined identity bases and explicit effect models, we derive and certify six classification cells in Lean 4 for scope decomposition, rule refinement, and forking. The derivations show how classifications depend on field granularity, admissible transformation steps, and explicit continuity warrants.
  We also characterize the identity relations generated by invariant-preserving steps. Two bases generate equal relations exactly when they agree on the preservation of every admissible step in a shared comparison domain, and a single separating step witnesses a difference.
  The formalization makes identity claims auditable, provides testable conditions for systems that transform records, and exposes the assumptions behind each classification. The results are conditional on the declared bases, models, and warrants, whose adequacy for particular referents requires independent justification.

title: Jacobian Scopes: A Unified Geometric Framework for Token-Level LLM Attribution
summary: Large language models (LLMs) make next-token predictions based on clues present in their context, such as semantic descriptions and in-context examples. Yet, elucidating which prior tokens most strongly influence a given prediction remains challenging due to the proliferation of layers and attention heads in modern architectures. We propose Jacobian Scopes, a suite of gradient-based, token level causal attribution methods for interpreting LLM predictions. Grounded in perturbation theory and information geometry, Jacobian Scopes quantify how input tokens influence various aspects of a model's prediction, such as specific logits, the full predictive distribution, and model uncertainty (effective temperature). Through case studies spanning instruction understanding, translation, and in-context learning (ICL), we demonstrate how Jacobian Scopes reveal implicit political biases, uncover word- and phrase-level translation strategies, and shed light on recently debated mechanisms underlying in-context time-series forecasting. On token-ablation faithfulness benchmarks (LAMBADA and IWSLT2017) across six LLMs, the distribution-level Fisher and Temperature Scopes significantly outperform established gradient-based attribution methods in 10 of 12 model-dataset settings. To facilitate exploration of Jacobian Scopes on custom text, we open-source our implementations and provide a cloud-hosted interactive demo at https://huggingface.co/spaces/Typony/JacobianScopes.

title: Multigrade Neural Network Approximation
summary: We study multigrade deep learning (MGDL) as a principled framework for structured error refinement in deep neural networks. While the approximation power of neural networks is now relatively well understood, training very deep architectures remains challenging due to highly nonconvex and often ill-conditioned optimization landscapes. In contrast, for relatively shallow networks, most notably certain one-hidden-layer ReLU models, training admits convex reformulations with global guarantees under appropriate settings, motivating learning paradigms that improve stability while scaling to depth. MGDL builds on this insight by training deep networks grade by grade: previously learned grades are frozen, and each newly added grade-wise subnetwork is composed on top of the previously learned grades and trained to fit the residual left by the current approximation, yielding a structured and interpretable hierarchical refinement process. We develop an operator-theoretic foundation for MGDL and prove that, for any continuous target function defined on a hypercube, there exists a fixed-width multigrade ReLU scheme whose residuals are pointwise nonincreasing in magnitude and converge uniformly to zero, with strict $L^p$-norm decay at every nontrivial grade for $p\in [1,\infty)$. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous constructive approximation guarantee showing that a grade-wise residual refinement scheme can achieve vanishing error in a fixed-width multigrade ReLU architecture.

title: Stochstic Sampling for Generative Diffusion Models: From Euler-Maruyama to Higher-Order Schemes
summary: We develop a convergence analysis for generative diffusion models that simultaneously accounts for the three principal error sources in stochastic sampling: initialization, score matching, and discretization of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation (SDE). Our central tool is the notion of a iterative-wise general strong scheme, a broad class of discretization methods for the reverse dynamics defined via explicit, index-wise tolerances on their Itô--Taylor coefficients. This notion refines Kloeden and Platen's general strong schemes into an iterate-wise formulation whose per-step conditions imply the classical remainder bound. We prove a 2-Wasserstein convergence theorem that applies to this entire class, reducing the analysis of any concrete sampler to a finite checklist, and covers general forward processes with time-dependent, spatially linear drift and spatially independent diffusion coefficient. We focus on dissipative reverse-time SDEs, which allows us to relax the $T$-dependence of the discretization and score-matching errors from exponential to polynomial. We instantiate our theorem for Euler--Maruyama, the exponential integrator, and, as our main application, derivative-free stochastic Runge--Kutta schemes of strong order $1.5$. To our knowledge, these are the first full convergence guarantees for solvers whose strong order strictly exceeds that of Euler--Maruyama. We further derive the resulting iteration complexity and a parameter-selection rule for the terminal time, score accuracy, and step size. Numerical experiments on Gaussian toy models and CIFAR-10 are consistent with the predicted convergence orders, and on ImageNet, out-of-the-box higher-order SDE solvers can yield substantial speed-ups, requiring at least four times fewer score evaluations than Euler--Maruyama. Code available at: https://github.com/emanuelpfarr/SSGDM.

title: Sampling Sphere Packings with Continuum Glauber Dynamics
comments: 85 pages, 1 figure. Fixed typos, streamlined proofs and added references. Extended main result from R^d to complete separable metric spaces. Accepted to SODA 2027
summary:
Continuum Glauber dynamics is a spatial birth-death process whose stationary distribution is a Gibbs distribution. We establish a spectral gap for Continuum Glauber dynamics applied to Gibbs point processes with repulsive pair potentials, a well-known special case of which is the hard sphere model. For arbitrary-range repulsive pair potentials, we show that a continuous version of Spectral Independence suffices to establish a spectral gap. This extends the regime of activity for which Continuum Glauber dynamics is known to mix, yielding a simple efficient sampling algorithm for arbitrary-range pair potentials that matches the known efficient sampling regime for finite-range pair potentials currently based on specialized algorithms. As a consequence, we also improve the threshold up to which packings of fixed size/density can be efficiently sampled from a bounded domain, the first improvement since Kannan, Mahoney and Montenegro (2003).
  To prove these results, we develop continuous analogs of Spectral Independence and negative fields localization. We show that a stronger variant of zero-freeness implies Spectral Independence, which in turn allows us to run the localization scheme to boost the spectral gap of Continuum Glauber dynamics from smaller activity to larger activity. While this follows the high-level blueprint of Chen and Eldan (2022) for the discrete setting, we have to address several novel difficulties due to the continuous setting. Notably, we avoid discretization in the algorithm and the analysis and work directly in the continuous setting.

title: Neural Neural Scaling Laws
summary: Neural scaling laws predict how language model performance improves with increased training inputs. While aggregate metrics like validation loss can follow smooth power-law curves, individual downstream tasks exhibit diverse scaling behaviors: some improve monotonically, others plateau, and some even degrade with scale. We argue that predicting downstream performance from validation loss suffers from two limitations: averaging token-level losses obscures signal, and no simple parametric family can capture the full spectrum of scaling behaviors. To address this, we propose Neural Neural Scaling Laws (NeuNeu), a neural network that frames scaling law prediction as time-series extrapolation. NeuNeu combines temporal context from observed accuracy trajectories with token-level validation losses, learning to predict future performance without the limitations inherent in assuming a specific functional form. Trained entirely on open-source model checkpoints from HuggingFace, NeuNeu achieves 1.99% mean absolute error in predicting model accuracy on 66 downstream tasks -- a 44% reduction compared to logistic scaling laws (3.56% MAE). Furthermore, NeuNeu generalizes zero-shot to unseen model families, architectures, parameter counts, and downstream tasks. Our work suggests that predicting downstream scaling directly from data outperforms parametric alternatives.

title: A Scalable Multi-Task Model for Virtual Sensors
summary: Virtual sensors replace expensive physical sensors in critical applications through machine learning by predicting target signals from available measurements. Existing virtual sensor approaches require application-specific models with hand-selected inputs for each sensor, cannot leverage task synergies, and lack consistent benchmarks. While emerging time series foundation models offer general-purpose, pretrained solutions in other domains, they are computationally expensive and limited to predicting their input signals, making them incompatible with virtual sensors. We introduce the first multi-task model for virtual sensors addressing both limitations. Our unified model can simultaneously predict diverse virtual sensors exploiting synergies while maintaining computational efficiency. It learns relevant input signals for each virtual sensor, eliminating expert knowledge requirements while adding explainability. In our large-scale evaluation on three standard benchmarks and an application-specific dataset with over 18 billion samples, our architecture reduces computation time by up to 415x and memory requirements by 951x, while maintaining or even improving predictive quality compared to unified baselines. Compared to existing isolated models for a single virtual sensor, our unified approach generates superior predictions at similar inference speed while scaling gracefully to hundreds of virtual sensors with nearly constant parameter count, enabling practical deployment in large-scale sensor networks.

title: LoRIF: Pushing the Scalability Frontier of Training Data Attribution
summary: Training data attribution (TDA) identifies which training examples most influenced a model's prediction. Influence function methods are a theoretically grounded family of TDA methods and exploit gradients. To overcome the scalability challenge arising from gradient computation, the most popular strategy is random projection (e.g., TRAK, LoGRA). However, this still faces two bottlenecks when scaling to large training sets and high-quality attribution: \emph{(i)} storing and loading projected per-example gradients for all $N$ training examples, where query latency is dominated by I/O; and \emph{(ii)} forming the $D \times D$ inverse Hessian approximation, which costs $O(D^2)$ memory. Both bottlenecks scale with the projection dimension $D$, yet increasing $D$ is necessary for attribution quality -- creating a quality--scalability tradeoff. We introduce \textbf{LoRIF} (\textbf{Lo}w-\textbf{R}ank \textbf{I}nfluence \textbf{F}unctions), which exploits low-rank structures of gradient to address both bottlenecks. First, we store rank-$c$ factors of projected per-example gradients rather than full matrices, reducing storage and query-time I/O from $O(D)$ to $O(c\sqrt{D})$ per layer per sample. Second, we use truncated SVD with the Woodbury identity to approximate the inverse Hessian term in an $r$-dimensional subspace, reducing memory from $O(D^2)$ to $O(Dr)$. On models from 0.1B to 70B parameters trained on datasets with millions of examples, LoRIF achieves up to 20$\times$ storage reduction and query-time speedup compared to LoGRA, while matching or exceeding its attribution quality. LoRIF makes gradient-based TDA practical at frontier scale. Code is available at https://github.com/doub7e/LoRIF.

title: Industrialized Deception: The Collateral Effects of LLM-Generated Misinformation on Digital Ecosystems
comments: 8 pages, 2 figures. Published in the Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW Companion '26), pp. 295-302
summary:
Generative AI and misinformation research have evolved since our 2024 survey. This paper presents an updated perspective, transitioning from literature review to practical countermeasures. We report on changes in the threat landscape, including improved AI-generated content through Large Language Models (LLMs) and multimodal systems - addressing the adverse impacts of AI on information quality.
  This work focuses on our practical contributions: JudgeGPT, a platform to evaluate human perception of AI-generated news, and RogueGPT, a controlled stimulus generation engine for research. Together, these tools form an experimental pipeline for studying how humans perceive and detect AI-generated misinformation.
  Our findings show that detection capabilities have improved, but competition between generation and detection continues. We discuss mitigation strategies such as LLM-based detection, inoculation approaches, and the dual-use nature of generative AI.

title: Defining Operational Conditions for Safety-Critical AI-Based Systems from Data
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been on the rise in many domains, including numerous safety-critical applications. However, for complex systems in the real world, defining the underlying environmental conditions in which the AI-based system must operate---the Operational Design Domain (ODD)---is extremely challenging. This often results in an incomplete description of the ODD, which contrasts with the requirements of many domains for certifying AI-based systems. Traditionally, the ODD is created in the early stages of the development process, drawing on sophisticated expert knowledge and related standards. This paper presents a novel method for defining the ODD a posteriori from previously collected data using a multidimensional kernel-based representation. This approach is validated through both synthetic benchmarks and a real-world aviation use case. Moreover, the paper defines similarity of two ODDs if they generate the same outputs up to Lebesgue-null input sets and proves convergence in volume of the calibrated representation under the stated assumptions. The novel, safety-by-design, deterministic kernel-based ODD representation is derived fully automatically, given documented assurance inputs, permutation-stable, bounded by construction, and, under affine-equivariant per-dimension normalization, invariant to the choice of units. Utilizing the proposed ODD representation supports future certification of data-driven, safety-critical AI-based systems.

title: Riemannian Lyapunov Framework: Optimization as Closed Loop Control on Riemannian Manifolds
summary: We introduce the Riemannian Lyapunov Framework (RLF), a unified framework that represents first order optimization as a closed loop controlled dynamical system on a Riemannian parameter manifold. Within this framework, optimizers are specified by a quadruple $(M, g, Φ, η)$ consisting of a Riemannian metric, an internal state transition map, a direction field generator, and a lifting parameter. Classical and modern methods including SGD, Adam, AdamW, Lion and Shampoo are recovered as specific instantiations of this quadruple. The central structural object of the framework is a time indexed family of target submanifolds in the extended state space of parameters, velocities, and internal memory, which we call the Normally Attracting Invariant Manifold (NAIM) family. These submanifolds organize training dynamics into two timescales: a fast contraction of the velocity state onto the current target submanifold, followed by a slow descent along it. Using Riemannian backstepping, we construct a strict Lyapunov function on the extended state space and prove Uniform Ultimate Boundedness (UUB) of the optimization trajectory under a descent alignment assumption and bounded stochastic disturbances. Under the additional Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition, the Lyapunov function converges linearly to a bounded neighborhood of the optimum, defined as the drift of the target direction field between consecutive iterates after parallel transport. To validate the framework's generativity, we derive three concrete instantiations of the quadruple, each exercising a distinct design axis, and show on geometric diagnostics, image classification benchmarks, and language modeling that their empirical behavior matches the theoretical predictions. The framework casts optimizer design as controller synthesis, complementing heuristic perspectives by providing a constructive template with provable guarantees.

title: Toward Autonomous Laboratory Safety Monitoring with Vision Language Models: Learning to See Hazards Through Scene Structure
summary: Laboratories are prone to severe injuries from unsafe actions, yet continuous manual safety monitoring, beyond mandatory pre-lab safety training, is infeasible. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer promise for autonomous laboratory safety monitoring, but their effectiveness in realistic settings is unclear due to the lack of visual evaluation data. Safety incidents are mostly documented as text, and existing studies are largely limited to textual understanding. Since hazardous scenes are unsafe to stage or capture, synthetic visual data becomes the only practical way to study this problem. This motivates us to introduce a structured data generation pipeline that converts textual laboratory scenarios into aligned quadruples using LLM as scene graph architect and image generation model as renderer, yielding \dataset: a synthetic dataset of 1,207 $\langle$image, scene graph, ground truth, hazard relevance mask$\rangle$ quadruples across 362 unique scenarios. Experiments on \dataset and seven open- and closed-source models show that VLMs perform effectively given a textual scene graph but degrade substantially in visual-only settings (i.e., where no scene graph is involved), indicating difficulty in extracting structured object relationships directly from pixels. We thus propose \saga, a post-training framework that leverages reinforcement learning to first structure the visual scene as a scene graph, and then predict hazards while aligning attention with relevant image regions. Evaluations with Qwen 3.5 and Gemma 4 show that our method nearly doubles the $F_1$ score over the baseline on our synthetic dataset and achieves an improvement of $\sim 3\times$ on a mini real-world dataset, while preserving general visual understanding in visual question answering.

title: PRISM: Festina Lente Proactivity -- Risk-Sensitive, Uncertainty-Aware Deliberation for Proactive Agents
summary: Proactive agents must decide not only what to say but also whether and when to intervene. Many current systems rely on brittle heuristics or indiscriminate long reasoning, which offers little control over the benefit-burden tradeoff. We formulate the problem as cost-sensitive selective intervention and present PRISM, a novel framework that couples a decision-theoretic gate with a dual-process reasoning architecture. At inference time, the agent intervenes only when a calibrated probability of user acceptance exceeds a threshold derived from asymmetric costs of missed help and false alarms. Inspired by festina lente (Latin: "make haste slowly"), we gate by an acceptance-calibrated, cost-derived threshold and invoke a resource-intensive Slow mode with counterfactual checks only near the decision boundary, concentrating computation on ambiguous and high-stakes cases. Training uses gate-aligned, schema-locked distillation: a teacher running the full PRISM pipeline provides dense, executable supervision on unlabeled interaction traces, while the student learns a response policy that is explicitly decoupled from the intervention gate to enable tunable and auditable control. On ProactiveBench, PRISM reduces false alarms by 22.78% and improves F1 by 20.14% over strong baselines. These results show that principled decision-theoretic gating, paired with selective slow reasoning and aligned distillation, yields proactive agents that are precise, computationally efficient, and controllable. To facilitate reproducibility, we release our code, models, and resources at https://prism-festinalente.github.io/; all experiments use the open-source ProactiveBench benchmark.

AI.title_translation: PRISM：欲速则不达的主动性——面向主动型智能体的风险敏感且不确定性感知深思框架
AI.tldr: PRISM通过将成本敏感的决策门控与按需触发的双系统深思推理相结合，实现了更精准、低误报且高效的主动型智能体干预。
AI.motivation: 主动型智能体不仅需要决定说什么，还需决定是否以及何时进行干预。现有系统通常依赖脆弱的启发式规则或不加区分的冗长推理，难以有效平衡干预收益与给用户带来的负担。
AI.method: 提出PRISM框架：1. 将问题形式化为成本敏感的选择性干预，利用校准的用户接受概率与基于非对称成本导出的阈值构建决策论门控；2. 采用双系统推理架构（践行“欲速则不达/festina lente”理念），仅在决策边界附近触发高计算开销的慢速模式及反事实检查；3. 采用门控对齐、模式锁定的知识蒸馏，由教师模型在无标签交互轨迹上提供监督，使学生模型学习与干预门控显式解耦的响应策略。
AI.result: 在ProactiveBench基准上，PRISM相比强基线模型将虚警率（误报）降低了22.78%，并将F1分数提升了20.14%。
AI.conclusion: 原则性的决策论门控与选择性慢思考推理及对齐蒸馏相结合，能够使主动型智能体兼具精准性、计算高效性与可控性。
AI.translation: 主动型智能体不仅必须决定说什么，还必须决定是否以及何时进行干预。目前许多系统依赖脆弱的启发式方法或不加区分的长链推理，这在收益与打扰负担之间的权衡上几乎无法提供控制。我们将该问题形式化为成本敏感的选择性干预，并提出了PRISM——一个将决策论门控与双系统推理架构相结合的新型框架。在推理时，仅当经过校准的用户接受概率超过根据遗漏帮助与误报的非对称成本推导出的阈值时，智能体才会介入。受“欲速则不达”（festina lente）理念的启发，我们通过经接受度校准且由成本导出的阈值进行门控，并仅在决策边界附近调用包含反事实检查的高资源开销“慢速模式”，从而将计算资源集中在模棱两可和高风险的情况上。训练过程采用门控对齐、模式锁定的蒸馏方法：运行完整PRISM流程的教师模型在无标签的交互轨迹上提供密集的、可执行的监督，而学生模型学习与干预门控显式解耦的响应策略，从而实现可调且可审计的控制。在ProactiveBench基准上，PRISM相比强基线模型将虚警率降低了22.78%，F1值提高了20.14%。这些结果表明，原则性的决策论门控配合选择性慢思考推理和对齐蒸馏，能够产生精准、计算高效且可控的主动型智能体。为促进可复现性，我们在 https://prism-festinalente.github.io/ 开源了代码、模型和资源；所有实验均基于开源的ProactiveBench基准。
AI.summary: 本研究针对主动型智能体在决定是否干预时难以权衡收益与打扰负担的问题，提出了PRISM框架。该框架结合了基于成本敏感的决策论门控与双系统推理架构，仅在校准的接受概率超过特定成本阈值时进行干预，并在决策边界附近调用高开销的慢思考与反事实检查，同时采用解耦的门控对齐蒸馏技术。实验表明PRISM能显著降低误报并提高干预准确率。
AI.keywords: 主动型智能体 (Proactive Agents), 决策论门控 (Decision-Theoretic Gating), 双系统推理 (Dual-Process Reasoning), 成本敏感干预 (Cost-Sensitive Intervention), 知识蒸馏 (Distillation)
AI.comments: PRISM创新性地将决策论中的成本敏感控制与认知科学的双系统推理架构相结合，提出了一种基于校准概率和非对称成本阈值的主动干预机制，既避免了频繁打扰用户（降低误报），又在不确定性高的边界情况下合理分配计算资源进行反事实反思。这种将干预决策门控与响应策略显式解耦的蒸馏方法，也极大提高了系统的可控性与可审计性。

title: Spectral-Aligned Pruning for Universal Error-Correcting Code Transformers
summary: Universal channel decoders based on transformers-such as the Foundation Error Correction Code Transformer (FECCT)-achieve competitive decoding performance across diverse code families with a single shared backbone, optionally followed by code-specific finetuning. However, the high computational complexity and large parameter footprint of FECCT present substantial obstacles to practical deployment. To address these challenges, we investigate structured pruning for FECCT and propose Spectral-Aligned Pruning (SAP), a structure-aware framework that enables cross-code reuse of structured pruning masks by leveraging the spectrum of the corresponding bipartite graph. SAP is grounded in classical graph analysis of codes: the two algebraically largest adjacency eigenvalues provide compact spectral proxies for degree scale, expansion ratio, and minimum-distance lower bounds. These quantities are directly relevant to decoding performance: degree scale reflects how densely codeword bits and parity checks are connected; expansion ratio influences how information propagates across the bipartite graph; and minimum distance characterizes codeword separation. Based on this connection, SAP uses these two leading eigenvalues as a lightweight code signature for pruning-mask retrieval. Empirically, this two-dimensional signature yields stable library selection equivalent to higher-dimensional spectral signatures in our evaluation. After pruning, SAP uses parameter-efficient low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to recover decoding performance while storing only a small number of additional adapter parameters per code. Experiments across diverse codes show that SAP achieves decoding performance comparable to dedicated per-code pruning, while enabling substantial reductions in computational cost and model memory footprint through kernel-level structured pruning. Code is available at https://github.com/iil-postech/sap.

AI.title_translation: 面向通用纠错码Transformer的谱对齐剪枝
AI.tldr: 本文提出谱对齐剪枝（SAP），利用二分图的谱特征实现剪枝掩码跨码复用，显著降低通用纠错码Transformer的计算和内存开销。
AI.motivation: 基于Transformer的通用信道译码器（如FECCT）虽然在多种码族上性能优异，但其巨大的参数量和高计算复杂度严重阻碍了在实际通信系统中的部署。
AI.method: 提出了结构感知的“谱对齐剪枝（SAP）”框架：1）利用纠错码对应二分图邻接矩阵中代数最大的两个特征值作为紧凑的二维码签名（代表度规模、扩展比和最小距离下界），用于跨码型检索与复用结构化剪枝掩码；2）在剪枝后，引入参数高效的低秩自适应（LoRA）技术，每个码仅需微量额外适配器参数即可恢复译码性能。
AI.result: 实验表明，二维谱签名能够实现与高维签名等效的稳定掩码库检索；在多种不同码型上，SAP通过内核级结构化剪枝大幅降低了计算量和内存占用，且译码性能与针对单一码专门训练的独立剪枝相当。
AI.conclusion: SAP成功利用二分图的紧凑谱特征实现了结构化剪枝掩码在不同信道码之间的有效复用，为通用纠错码Transformer提供了一种高效、低存储开销且性能无损的轻量化部署解决方案。
AI.translation: 基于Transformer的通用信道译码器（例如基础纠错码Transformer，FECCT）利用单一共享骨干网络在多种不同码族上取得了极具竞争力的译码性能，并可选择在特定码上进行微调。然而，FECCT极高的计算复杂度和庞大的参数规模为其在实际中的部署带来了巨大阻碍。为了解决这些挑战，我们研究了FECCT的结构化剪枝，并提出了“谱对齐剪枝”（SAP）——一种结构感知框架，通过利用对应二分图的谱特征实现结构化剪枝掩码的跨码复用。SAP植根于经典的码图分析：两个代数最大的邻接特征值为度规模、扩展比以及最小距离下界提供了紧凑的谱代理。这些量与译码性能直接相关：度规模反映了码字比特与奇偶校验的连接稠密程度；扩展比影响信息在二分图上的传播方式；而最小距离表征了码字的分离程度。基于这种联系，SAP采用这两个主特征值作为轻量级码签名进行剪枝掩码检索。实验表明，在我们的评估中，这种二维签名可以产生与高维谱签名相当的稳定库选择。剪枝后，SAP利用参数高效的低秩自适应（LoRA）来恢复译码性能，每个码仅需存储少量的额外适配器参数。在多种码上的实验表明，SAP取得了与针对特定码专门剪枝相当的译码性能，同时通过内核级结构化剪枝大幅降低了计算成本和模型内存占用。代码可在 https://github.com/iil-postech/sap 获取。
AI.summary: 本文针对通用纠错码Transformer（FECCT）计算开销大、难以部署的问题，提出了谱对齐剪枝（SAP）。该方法将信道码二分图的前两大特征值作为轻量级签名来检索和复用结构化剪枝掩码，并结合LoRA高效恢复性能，在显著降低模型计算与内存开销的同时，保持了与单独逐码剪枝相当的译码性能。
AI.keywords: 纠错码 (Error-Correcting Code), Transformer, 结构化剪枝 (Structured Pruning), 谱分析 (Spectral Analysis), 低秩自适应 (LoRA)
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将经典信道编码理论中的二分图谱分析引入深度学习模型的模型压缩领域。通过证明图邻接矩阵的前两大特征值与编码的关键性能指标（度规模、扩展比、最小距离）之间的内在联系，提出了极具物理与数学解释性的剪枝掩码跨码复用机制，避免了为每个新码型重新搜索剪枝结构的巨大成本。结合LoRA技术，兼顾了压缩率与译码精度，为轻量化通用译码器的工程落地提供了切实可行的方案。

title: ClueTracer: Question-to-Vision Clue Tracing for Training-Free Hallucination Suppression in Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Large multimodal reasoning models solve challenging visual problems via explicit long-chain inference: they gather visual clues from images and decode clues into textual tokens. Yet this capability also increases hallucinations, where the model generates content that is not supported by the input image or the question. To understand this failure mode, we identify \emph{reasoning drift}: during clue gathering, the model over-focuses on question-irrelevant entities, diluting focus on task-relevant cues and gradually decoupling the reasoning trace from visual grounding. As a consequence, many inference-time localization or intervention methods developed for non-reasoning models fail to pinpoint the true clues in reasoning settings. Motivated by these insights, we introduce ClueRecall, a metric for assessing visual clue retrieval, and present ClueTracer, a training-free, parameter-free, and architecture-agnostic plugin for hallucination suppression. ClueTracer starts from the question and traces how key clues propagate along the model's reasoning pathway (question $\rightarrow$ outputs $\rightarrow$ visual tokens), thereby localizing task-relevant patches while suppressing spurious attention to irrelevant regions. Remarkably, \textbf{without any additional training}, ClueTracer improves all \textbf{reasoning} architectures (including \texttt{R1-OneVision}, \texttt{Ocean-R1}, \texttt{MM-Eureka}, \emph{etc}.) by $\mathbf{1.21\times}$ on reasoning benchmarks

AI.title_translation: ClueTracer：用于多模态推理中免训练幻觉抑制的问题到视觉线索追踪
AI.tldr: 提出免训练插件 ClueTracer，通过沿推理路径追踪关键线索来定位相关视觉区域并抑制幻觉，在推理基准上实现各类多模态推理模型 1.21 倍的性能提升。
AI.motivation: 大型多模态推理模型在长链推理中容易出现“推理漂移”——即在提取线索时过度关注与问题无关的实体，稀释对任务相关线索的专注度，导致推理轨迹逐渐与视觉扎根脱节并产生幻觉，而现存针对非推理模型的干预方法无法在该场景下精确定位有效线索。
AI.method: 提出评估视觉线索检索能力的指标 ClueRecall，并设计了免训练、无参数且跨架构的即插即用插件 ClueTracer。该方法从问题出发，沿着模型推理路径（问题 $\rightarrow$ 输出 $\rightarrow$ 视觉标记）追踪关键线索的传播过程，以此定位与任务相关的图像块并抑制对无关区域的虚假注意力。
AI.result: 在完全不需要额外训练的情况下，ClueTracer 在推理基准测试中使所有受测推理架构（包括 R1-OneVision、Ocean-R1、MM-Eureka 等）的性能均提升了 1.21 倍。
AI.conclusion: ClueTracer 成功揭示并缓解了多模态长链推理中的推理漂移问题，证明了通过追踪问题到视觉的线索传播路径能够有效重构视觉扎根，为免训练的多模态幻觉抑制提供了行之有效的新范式。
AI.translation: 大型多模态推理模型通过显式长链推理来解决复杂的视觉问题：它们从图像中收集视觉线索，并将线索解码为文本标记。然而，这种能力也加剧了幻觉现象，即模型生成了输入图像或问题所不支持的内容。为了理解这种失效模式，我们指出了“推理漂移”（reasoning drift）：在收集线索期间，模型过度关注与问题无关的实体，稀释了对任务相关线索的专注度，并使推理轨迹逐渐与视觉扎根脱钩。因此，许多为非推理模型开发的推理期定位或干预方法在推理场景中难以精确定位真实线索。基于这些见解，我们引入了用于评估视觉线索检索的指标 ClueRecall，并提出了 ClueTracer——一种用于幻觉抑制的免训练、无参数且跨架构通用的插件。ClueTracer 从问题出发，追踪关键线索如何沿着模型的推理路径（问题 $\rightarrow$ 输出 $\rightarrow$ 视觉标记）进行传播，从而在抑制对无关区域的虚假注意力的同时定位任务相关的图像块。值得注意的是，在无需任何额外训练的情况下，ClueTracer 在推理基准上将所有推理架构（包括 R1-OneVision、Ocean-R1、MM-Eureka 等）的表现提升了 1.21 倍。
AI.summary: 本研究发现了多模态推理模型中长链推理易引发“推理漂移”进而导致视觉脱钩与幻觉的机制。为此，作者提出了线索检索评估指标 ClueRecall 与免训练插件 ClueTracer，通过追踪从问题经由输出至视觉标记的线索传播路径，有效滤除虚假注意力并定位关键图像区域，在多类主流多模态推理模型上实现了显著的幻觉抑制与性能增益。
AI.keywords: 多模态推理, 幻觉抑制, 推理漂移, 线索追踪, 免训练方法
AI.comments: 该工作深入揭示了多模态长思维链推理特有的“推理漂移”现象，指出了传统针对非推理模型的幻觉干预手段在长链场景下的失效。提出的 ClueTracer 采用“问题-输出-视觉”的反向/前向传播追踪线索，具备无参数、免训练和跨模型架构的极高实用价值；局限在于摘要未披露追踪过程对推理延迟和计算资源开销的具体影响。

title: The Verification Crisis: Expert Perceptions of GenAI Disinformation and the Case for Reproducible Provenance
comments: 9 pages. Author version; the Version of Record appeared in the Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW '26 Companion), pp. 980-988
summary: The growth of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has shifted disinformation production from manual fabrication to automated, large-scale manipulation. This article presents findings from the first wave of a longitudinal expert perception survey (N=21) involving AI researchers, policymakers, and disinformation specialists. It examines the perceived severity of multimodal threats -- text, image, audio, and video -- and evaluates current mitigation strategies. Results indicate that while deepfake video presents immediate "shock" value, large-scale text generation poses a systemic risk of "epistemic fragmentation" and "synthetic consensus," particularly in the political domain. The survey reveals skepticism about technical detection tools, with experts favoring provenance standards and regulatory frameworks despite implementation barriers. GenAI disinformation research requires reproducible methods. The current challenge is measurement: without standardized benchmarks and reproducibility checklists, tracking or countering synthetic media remains difficult. We propose treating information integrity as an infrastructure with rigor in data provenance and methodological reproducibility.
comment: 9 pages. Author version; the Version of Record appeared in the Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW '26 Companion), pp. 980-988

AI.title_translation: 验证危机：专家对生成式人工智能虚假信息的看法与可复现出处追踪的必要性
AI.tldr: 专家调查表明，大规模文本生成比深度伪造视频更具系统性威胁，技术检测难以独力应对，必须依靠可复现的数据出处追踪与基础设施级治理。
AI.motivation: 生成式人工智能使得虚假信息的制造由人工捏造演变为自动化、大规模的操纵，引发了验证危机，亟需厘清不同多模态威胁的严重程度并评估现有治理策略。
AI.method: 开展了一项纵向专家认知调查的第一阶段研究（样本量 N=21），受访对象涵盖人工智能研究人员、政策制定者以及虚假信息领域的专家。
AI.result: 深度伪造视频主要带来即时的感官冲击，而大规模文本生成则在政治等领域引发“认识碎片化”和“虚假共识”的系统性风险；专家对技术性检测工具持怀疑态度，更青睐出处标准和监管框架；当前的核心困难在于缺乏标准化基准和可复现性清单等衡量工具。
AI.conclusion: 生成式人工智能虚假信息研究亟需可复现的方法。应对合成媒体的挑战需要将信息完整性视为一种基础设施，并在数据出处追踪和方法可复现性方面建立严格的标准。
AI.translation: 生成式人工智能（GenAI）的发展已将虚假信息的生产从人工捏造转变为自动化、大规模的操纵。本文展示了一项针对人工智能研究人员、政策制定者和虚假信息专家的纵向专家认知调查第一阶段（N=21）的发现。本研究探讨了文本、图像、音频和视频等多模态威胁的感知严重程度，并评估了当前的缓解策略。结果表明，虽然深度伪造视频具有即时的“震惊”效应，但大规模文本生成在政治领域带来了“认识碎片化”和“合成共识”的系统性风险。调查显示专家对纯技术检测工具持怀疑态度，尽管存在实施障碍，他们仍更倾向于出处标准和监管框架。生成式人工智能虚假信息研究需要可复现的方法。当前的挑战在于度量：若没有标准化的基准和可复现性检查清单，追踪或对抗合成媒体仍然十分困难。我们主张将信息完整性视为一种基础设施，并在数据出处和方法可复现性上保持严格标准。
AI.summary: 本文通过对21位专家的调查，评估了生成式人工智能虚假信息的多模态威胁。结果表明，相比视频深度伪造，大规模文本生成的系统性风险更严重；专家普遍质疑检测工具的有效性，强调必须建立数据出处追踪机制与可复现基准，将信息完整性作为基础设施进行治理。
AI.keywords: 生成式人工智能, 虚假信息, 出处追踪, 可复现性, 深度伪造
AI.comments: 该研究的重要价值在于揭示了大规模文本生成相比视觉深度伪造具有更隐蔽、更具系统性的危害（如认知碎片化与虚假共识），并直击当前纯技术检测手段的局限性，倡导将信息真实性提升至基础设施与出处追踪层面。其局限在于作为第一阶段调查，专家样本量较小（N=21），结论的广泛代表性仍需后续纵向研究进一步验证。

title: Origin Lens: A Privacy-First Mobile Framework for Cryptographic Image Provenance and AI Detection
comments: 8 pages. Peer-reviewed and accepted at the FIIR Workshop, The Web Conference 2026; the workshop was cancelled and the paper is not included in the proceedings. A separate, independent paper on Origin Lens appeared at ACM WebSci '26: doi:10.1145/3795513.3806658
summary: The proliferation of generative AI poses challenges for information integrity assurance, requiring systems that connect model governance with end-user verification. We present Origin Lens, a privacy-first mobile framework that targets visual disinformation through a layered verification architecture. Unlike server-side detection systems, Origin Lens performs cryptographic image provenance verification and metadata-based AI detection locally on the device via a Rust/Flutter hybrid architecture. Our system integrates multiple signals - including cryptographic provenance, generative-model metadata and watermarks, and optional retrieval-augmented verification - to provide users with graded confidence indicators at the point of consumption. We discuss the framework's alignment with regulatory requirements (EU AI Act, DSA) and its role in verification infrastructure that complements platform-level mechanisms.

title: X2HDR: HDR Image Generation in a Perceptually Uniform Space
summary: High-dynamic-range (HDR) formats and displays are becoming increasingly prevalent, yet state-of-the-art image generators (e.g., Stable Diffusion and FLUX) typically remain limited to low-dynamic-range (LDR) output due to the lack of large-scale HDR training data. In this work, we show that existing pretrained diffusion models can be easily adapted to HDR generation without retraining from scratch. A key challenge is that HDR images are natively represented in linear RGB, whose intensity and color statistics differ substantially from those of sRGB-encoded LDR images. This gap, however, can be effectively bridged by converting HDR inputs into perceptually uniform encodings (e.g., using PU21 or PQ). Empirically, we find that LDR-pretrained variational autoencoders (VAEs) reconstruct PU21-encoded HDR inputs with fidelity comparable to LDR data, whereas linear RGB inputs cause severe degradations. Motivated by this finding, we describe an efficient adaptation strategy that freezes the VAE and finetunes only the denoiser via low-rank adaptation in a perceptually uniform space. This results in a unified computational method that supports both text-to-HDR synthesis and single-image RAW-to-HDR reconstruction. Experiments demonstrate that our perceptually encoded adaptation consistently improves perceptual fidelity, text-image alignment, and effective dynamic range, relative to previous techniques.

AI.title_translation: X2HDR：感知均匀空间中的高动态范围图像生成
AI.tldr: 利用感知均匀编码（如PU21）消除HDR与LDR的表征鸿沟，通过冻结VAE并仅微调去噪器，实现高效的文生HDR与RAW转HDR。
AI.motivation: HDR显示设备日趋普及，但由于缺乏大规模HDR训练数据，顶尖图像生成模型大多仅能输出LDR图像；且原生HDR的线性RGB与sRGB LDR在统计特性上差异巨大，从头训练代价极高。
AI.method: 将HDR输入转换为感知均匀编码（如PU21或PQ），以契合LDR预训练VAE的特性；在感知均匀空间中冻结预训练VAE，仅通过低秩适应（LoRA）微调去噪网络（Denoiser），构建出统一支持文本生成HDR（text-to-HDR）以及单图RAW转HDR（RAW-to-HDR）的高效适配方法。
AI.result: 实验表明，相比以往技术，基于感知均匀编码的适配策略在感知保真度、文本-图像对齐度以及有效动态范围方面均取得了持续显著的提升。
AI.conclusion: 通过将HDR数据映射到感知均匀空间，现有的预训练LDR扩散模型无需从头训练即可高效适配到HDR图像生成任务，并在感知保真度与动态范围上取得优异表现。
AI.translation: 高动态范围（HDR）格式与显示设备日益普及，然而由于缺乏大规模HDR训练数据，当前最先进的图像生成器（如Stable Diffusion和FLUX）通常仍受限于低动态范围（LDR）输出。在本文中，我们展示了现有的预训练扩散模型无需从头重新训练即可轻松适配到HDR生成任务。一个核心挑战在于HDR图像原生采用线性RGB表示，其亮度和色彩统计特性与sRGB编码的LDR图像存在显著差异。然而，通过将HDR输入转换为感知均匀编码（例如使用PU21或PQ），可以有效弥合这一差距。实验发现，经LDR预训练的变分自编码器（VAE）重建PU21编码的HDR输入时，保真度与LDR数据相当，而线性RGB输入则会导致严重的画质退化。基于这一发现，我们提出了一种高效的适配策略：冻结VAE，并在感知均匀空间中仅通过低秩适应（LoRA）微调去噪器。由此形成了一种统一的计算方法，可同时支持文本到HDR的合成以及单图像RAW到HDR的重建。实验表明，与先前的技术相比，我们基于感知编码的适配方法持续提升了感知保真度、图文对齐度以及有效动态范围。
AI.summary: 本文提出X2HDR，一种利用感知均匀编码将预训练LDR扩散模型适配为HDR生成模型的方法。通过冻结预训练VAE并仅用LoRA微调去噪器，该方法以低计算成本实现了高质量的文本到HDR生成与RAW到HDR重建。
AI.keywords: 高动态范围图像 (HDR), 扩散模型 (Diffusion Models), 感知均匀空间 (Perceptually Uniform Space), 低秩适应 (LoRA), 图像生成 (Image Generation)
AI.comments: 该工作创新性地发现感知均匀编码（如PU21）能够有效弥合线性RGB HDR与sRGB LDR之间的分布鸿沟，使预训练LDR VAE无需重新训练即可复用。结合LoRA的高效微调策略，为低成本将前沿文生图模型拓展至HDR领域提供了极具实用价值的方案。其局限在于摘要未详细说明微调所需的HDR数据规模以及极端光照场景下的泛化表现。

title: Learning Where It Matters: Geometric Anchoring for Robust Preference Alignment
summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and related methods align large language models from pairwise preferences by regularizing updates against a fixed reference policy. As the policy drifts, a static reference, however, can become increasingly miscalibrated, leading to distributional mismatch and amplifying spurious preference signals under noisy supervision. Conversely, reference-free variants avoid mismatch but often suffer from unconstrained reward drift. We propose Geometric Anchor Preference Optimization (GAPO), which replaces the fixed reference with a dynamic, geometry-aware anchor: an adversarial local perturbation of the current policy within a small radius that serves as a pessimistic baseline. This anchor enables an adaptive reweighting mechanism, modulating the importance of each preference pair based on its local sensitivity. We further introduce the Anchor Gap, the reward discrepancy between the policy and its anchor, and show under smoothness conditions that it approximates worst-case local margin degradation. Optimizing a logistic objective weighted by this gap downweights geometrically brittle instances while emphasizing robust preference signals. Across diverse noise settings, GAPO consistently improves robustness while matching or improving performance on standard LLM alignment and reasoning benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: 关键处学习：用于鲁棒偏好对齐的几何锚定
AI.tldr: 提出GAPO方法，利用局部对抗扰动构建动态几何锚点，并通过自适应加权下调脆弱样本权重，显著提升了大模型偏好对齐在噪声环境下的鲁棒性。
AI.motivation: DPO等方法依赖固定参考策略，随着策略漂移会导致分布失配并在噪声监督下放大伪偏好信号；而无参考变体虽然避免了失配，但易引发无约束的奖励漂移。因此需要一种兼顾防止漂移与避免失配的鲁棒对齐机制。
AI.method: 提出几何锚定偏好优化（GAPO），使用小半径内的对抗性局部扰动作为动态、感知几何的悲观锚点替代静态参考策略；提出“锚点差距”（Anchor Gap，策略与锚点之间的奖励差异）来度量局部敏感性与边距退化；利用该差距自适应调节样本权重，降低几何脆弱样本权重并强化鲁棒偏好信号。
AI.result: 在多种噪声设定下，GAPO一致性地提升了对齐的鲁棒性，并在标准大语言模型对齐和推理基准上取得相当或更优的性能。
AI.conclusion: GAPO通过动态几何锚点和基于Anchor Gap的自适应重加权机制，有效克服了传统方法在噪声数据下的分布失配和奖励漂移问题，在确保基准性能的同时显著提升了大模型偏好对齐的鲁棒性。
AI.translation: 直接偏好优化（DPO）及相关方法通过针对固定的参考策略正则化更新，来基于成对偏好对齐大语言模型。然而，随着策略漂移，静态参考可能会愈发失准，导致分布失配并在噪声监督下放大伪偏好信号。相反，无参考变体虽然避免了失配，但往往面临无约束的奖励漂移问题。为此，我们提出了几何锚定偏好优化（GAPO），它用动态且具备几何感知能力的锚点取代了固定参考——即在小半径内对当前策略进行对抗性局部扰动，作为悲观基准。该锚点能够实现自适应重加权机制，根据每个偏好对的局部敏感性调节其重要程度。我们进一步引入了“锚点差距”（Anchor Gap），即策略与其锚点之间的奖励差异，并在光滑性条件下证明其逼近了最坏情况下的局部边距退化。通过优化以此差距加权的逻辑目标函数，能够降低几何脆弱实例的权重，同时强化鲁棒的偏好信号。在多种噪声设定下，GAPO持续提高了鲁棒性，同时在标准大语言模型对齐和推理基准上达到或提升了性能。
AI.summary: 本文提出了几何锚定偏好优化（GAPO），通过引入当前策略的局部对抗扰动作动态几何锚点，并基于策略与锚点间的“锚点差距”进行自适应加权，抑制几何脆弱和噪声样本的影响，有效解决了DPO的静态参考失配和无参考方法的奖励漂移问题，实现了高鲁棒的大模型偏好对齐。
AI.keywords: 偏好对齐 (Preference Alignment), 直接偏好优化 (DPO), 几何锚定 (Geometric Anchoring), 鲁棒性 (Robustness), 锚点差距 (Anchor Gap)
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地跳出了传统DPO对“静态参考策略”或“完全无参考策略”的路径依赖，引入了动态对抗局部扰动作为几何锚点，为解决偏好对齐中的分布失配与奖励漂移问题提供了新思路。将Anchor Gap与最坏情况边距退化理论相结合的加权设计兼具理论深度与实用性。潜在局限可能在于计算局部对抗扰动会带来额外的计算开销。

title: Echoes as Anchors: Probabilistic Costs and Attention Refocusing in LLM Reasoning
comments: ICLR 2026 (poster). Public on OpenReview since 2025-10-08: https://openreview.net/forum?id=vndn1Wrult. Code: https://github.com/hhh2210/echoes-as-anchors
summary: Recent work improves reasoning in large reasoning models (LRMs) by test-time scaling through self-consistency and parallel thinking, adding generic "thinking tokens", or presenting the question twice, as in re-reading (RE2). However, these approaches either inject task-agnostic tokens or mandate heuristics that do not explain, and often ignore, the spontaneous repetition that many LRMs exhibit at the head of their long chain-of-thought (CoT). In this work, we analyze and harness the model's tendency to restate the question, dubbed Echo of Prompt (EOP), as a front-loaded, compute-shaping mechanism, which can be viewed as self-generated prompt repetition inside the reasoning trace rather than in the input. Specifically, we formalize its probabilistic cost by casting echo removal as rejection-based conditioning, and define the Echo Likelihood Gap $Δ\mathcal{L}$ as a computable proxy linking early repetition to likelihood gains and downstream accuracy. We find that (1) in a causal intervention, reinserting an echo into failed GSM8K traces raises exact match by 7.9-10.4 points for two reasoning models but not for a non-reasoning base model; and (2) in length- and suffix-controlled likelihood analyses and layer-wise attention studies conducted to show that EOP's benefits go beyond verbosity, EOP increases answer to answer-prefix attention in middle layers, consistent with an attention refocusing mechanism. Building on these findings, we develop Echo-Distilled SFT (ED-SFT) to instill an "echo-then-reason" pattern through supervised finetuning, and training-free Echoic Prompting (EP) to re-ground the model mid-trace. We evaluate on GSM8K, MathQA, Hendrycks-MATH, AIME24, and MATH-500 under identical decoding settings and budgets, and find consistent gains over baselines, including thinking-token insertion. Our code is publicly released at https://github.com/hhh2210/echoes-as-anchors.
